result.topic_en: Calculations on an elliptic-integral conformal map with a change to complex variables p = x+yi, q = x−yi for a second-order PDE with boundary conditions on a rectangle x = ±a, y = ±b; series expansions involving (1−z²)^{-1/2}; and elementary integrals of products of sines and cosines.
result.transcription:
$x+yi = \int \frac{dz}{\sqrt{z(z-e^{4y})(z-e^{-4y})}}$
$p = x+yi$
$q = x-yi$
[-$\frac{\partial w}{\partial p}$-] $\frac{\partial w}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} + \frac{\partial w}{\partial q}$ $\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x^2} = \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} + 2\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p \partial q} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2}$
$\frac{\partial w}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial w}{\partial p} i - \frac{\partial w}{\partial q} i$ $\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial y^2} = -\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} + 2\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p \partial q} - \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2}$
$x = \pm a$ $\left(\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2}\right)$ [-...-] $+ (4r^2 + [-...-]\frac{2}{r^2}[?])\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p \partial q} = 0$
[-...-] $\left(\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2}\right) - (4r^2+2)\left(\partial_p + \partial_q\right)[?] \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p \partial q} = 0$ $\frac{\partial w}{\partial x}[?]$ $\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p\partial q}\left(4+\frac{2}{r^2}\right) - \frac{1}{r^2}\left(\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2}\right)$
$y = \pm b$ $-\left(\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2}\right) + (4r^2 - 2)\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p \partial q} = 0$

$\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p^2} - \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial q^2} = 0$ $| x = \pm a \quad y = \pm b$

$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-z^2}}(a_0 + a_1 z \quad \cdots \quad a_n)$
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-z^2}}(a_0 + a_1 \frac{1}{z} \quad \cdots \quad )$
[-$z^n$-] $(1-z^2)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \sum \frac{\Pi - \frac{1}{2}\,(-z^2)^{m+n}}{\Pi m\; \Pi - \frac{1}{2} - m}$
[-...-] $= z^{n+1}\left(\frac{1}{z^2} - 1\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} = i \sum \frac{\Pi - \frac{1}{2}\,(-z^2)^{n+1-m}}{\Pi m\; \Pi - \frac{1}{2} - m}$

$4\frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial p \partial q} = \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 w}{\partial y^2} = 4\mu^2 w$

$\int \cos\alpha x \cos\lambda x\, dx = \frac{\alpha \sin\alpha x \cos\lambda x - \lambda \sin\lambda x \cos\alpha x}{\alpha^2 - \lambda^2}$
$\int \sin\alpha x \cos\lambda x\, dx = \frac{-[(\alpha-\lambda)\cos(\alpha+\lambda)x + (\alpha+\lambda)\cos(\alpha-\lambda)x]}{2(\alpha^2-\lambda^2)} = \frac{-\alpha \cos\alpha x \cos\lambda x - \lambda \sin\alpha x \sin\lambda x}{\alpha^2 - \lambda^2}$
$\int \sin\alpha x \sin\lambda x\, dx = \frac{\frac{1}{2}[(\alpha+\lambda)\sin(\alpha-\lambda)x - (\alpha-\lambda)\sin(\alpha+\lambda)x]}{\alpha^2 - \lambda^2} = \frac{-\alpha \sin\lambda x \cos\alpha x + \lambda \sin\alpha x \cos\lambda x}{\alpha^2 - \lambda^2}$
